_meta.file: meps_2021.csv (meps_prepare.py of h233, h231, h229if1 and the h229 event files)
_meta.codebook: MEPS 2021 public-use file documentation; variable labels read from the SAS V9 files
_meta.STATUS: FILLED 28 September 2026 from the MEPS 2021 public-use files; variable names and labels read from the files.

design._verified: MEPS person weight PERWT21F, variance strata VARSTR, PSU VARPSU (PSU numbers repeat across strata, so nested). Persons with zero weight are out of scope and excluded from every domain by the ETL.

gender._note: No gender-identity item on the MEPS public-use file.

age._note: Age the last time eligible during the year, top-coded at 85.

phenotype_concepts._instruction: MEPS concepts are the person's reported conditions (Medical Conditions file, ICD10CDX: ICD-10-CM truncated to 3 characters on the public file), joined into CONDS by meps_prepare.py and matched by prefix. absentIsNegative: a condition not reported during the year counts as not reported.

headache_migraine.questionText: Headache or migraine condition: G43 migraine, G44 other headache syndromes, R51 headache.

dizziness_balance.questionText: Dizziness or vestibular condition: R42 dizziness and giddiness, H81 disorders of vestibular function, H82 vertiginous syndromes. H81/H82 do not appear on the public file (collapsed for confidentiality); R42 carries the arm.

hearing_difficulty.questionText: Hearing loss condition: H90 conductive and sensorineural, H91 other and unspecified hearing loss.

tinnitus.questionText: H93 other disorders of the ear, which includes tinnitus (H93.1). The public file truncates codes to 3 characters, so tinnitus cannot be separated from the other H93 conditions; this arm is broader than tinnitus.

sinus_condition.questionText: Sinusitis condition: J01 acute, J32 chronic sinusitis. J01 does not appear on the public file; J32 carries the arm.

recalcitrance_proxy._hint: MEPS could approximate recalcitrance (repeat antibiotic or steroid fills linked to sinusitis within the year); not built in this pass.

caveats: Conditions are household-reported and coded by AHRQ to ICD-10-CM. A condition record means it was reported during the year (as a reason for care, a disability day or a current condition), not that a clinician confirmed it.

Codes are truncated to three characters on the public file and rare codes are collapsed for confidentiality, so vestibular disorders (H81/H82), H90 hearing loss and acute sinusitis (J01) do not appear, and tinnitus cannot be separated from other H93 ear disorders.
Suppressed unless the unweighted denominator is at least 100, at least 30 sample persons are phenotype-positive, and the RSE is 30% or less.
2021 falls within the COVID-19 pandemic; health-care use may differ from 2019, so compare years with that in mind.

Sinusitis-care spending is the sum, over office-based, outpatient, emergency, inpatient and prescribed-medicine events linked to a sinusitis condition, of all payments for the event. An event also linked to another condition counts in full, so this is an upper bound on sinusitis-attributable spending. Home health events are not included (file not supplied).
Dollar figures are nominal 2021 dollars, not inflation-adjusted.

One sample adult accounts for about a quarter (24%) of the weighted 2021 spending total: four outpatient events of about $35,000 each, each linked to chronic sinusitis alone. Without that person the mean is about $645. The interval carries this; single-year spending on a condition this rare moves with a few people.

Spending for adults who also report headache or migraine is the pool the proposal's avoidable-cost question applies to; it is reported separately and is suppressed when too few people carry both conditions. It is not an estimate of avoidable or misattributed spending, which needs a clinical attribution rule.

eligibility.reason: Adults reporting a sinusitis condition: the proposal 3.1 'sinus headache' population. The headline figure is the share who also report headache or migraine; the dollar figures cover all of them, and separately those who also report headache or migraine.

phenotype_definition: Among adults reporting sinusitis, the share who also report a headache or migraine condition. Dollar figures: mean and national total spending (all payers) on care linked to sinusitis during the year, for all adults reporting sinusitis and for those who also report headache or migraine.
